name: TapTap CLI
description: TapTap developer-operations plugin, running your installed official taptap-cli: sign-in, game creation, store listings, package uploads, qualification, review and release, test plans, asset library, data metrics, player reviews. Credentials stay in the CLI; writes need confirmation.
whenToUse: Work in the TapTap developer backend: sign in, find IDs, create a game, edit store-listing fields and the main package, upload packages, fill qualification gaps, submit or withdraw a review, publish, manage test plans, search the asset library, query data metrics and read player reviews

list_tools.description: List the TapTap business operations this plugin can run. The catalogue is read live from the taptap-cli installed on this machine. Without `category`, returns the top-level commands with their descriptions and the global execution rules; with `category`, drills down one level at a time (for example `category:"asset-library"`, then `category:"asset-library ai-image"`). When unsure of a command name, pass a prefix to search with (for example `category:"up"`). Drilling into a command that has no subcommands returns the flags it accepts; for full parameter detail use `call_tool` with `args._help:true`.Commands this plugin deliberately leaves out: CLI self-update (update) and the raw auth login (use auth login-start / login-wait).

/properties/category.description: Command path or prefix. Takes what the previous listing returned and deepens it (e.g. "asset-library", "asset-library ai-image"); pass a prefix to search when the name is uncertain (e.g. "up"). Omit it for the top level.

call_tool.description: Run one TapTap business operation. `name` comes from list_tools. `developer_id`/`app_id` are scope fields passed directly (mapped to --dev-id/--app-id); every other business field goes into `data` as JSON; any other key is a control flag mirrored as --flag, validated by the CLI against the command's schema; positionals such as file paths go in `_positional`, and local paths must be relative to the session workdir (the CLI rejects absolute paths and ../ escapes). Writes need the user's consent: preview with dry_run:true, then the identical arguments with yes:true; the worker refuses a write carrying neither, and every write in a read-only session. Getting consent is your job; yes is not proof of it. The orchestrated login-start/login-wait pair is the login flow itself — the user authorizes in the browser — so it is exempt. Failures carry execution_state: not_executed = nothing took effect (safe to retry); unknown = a write may have applied — verify before retrying, never re-run.

/properties/name.description: Operation name from list_tools, for example 'app get-app-module'.

/properties/args.description: Operation arguments as a JSON object. developer_id/app_id are scope fields passed directly (mapped to --dev-id/--app-id); every other business field must go in `data` (a JSON object); any key other than scope and data is a control flag mirrored as --flag, validated by the CLI against the command's own schema. Keys beginning with `_` are plugin controls and never become flags: `_positional` (array of positional arguments such as file paths, which must be relative to the session workdir), `_help` (show that command's --help), `_timeout_seconds` (per-call timeout in seconds, max 870, for long uploads). When unsure, drill down with list_tools first.
